about: Base components for agent-built UI. Rust validates trees against this file (src-tauri/src/ui_library.rs) and React renders them (src/components/ui-render.tsx). Keep the two in step when adding one. Each primitive lists the libraries it is built on in `uses`; a component's libraries are the union over the primitives it contains. Expanded (the Expand button, F), the UI fills a large dialog: `textfile`, `filetree`, `json`, `table`, `gitgraph`, `gitstatus`, `diffstat`, `wordcount` and `diffreview` give their main scroll area all the height left, with no cap. For any other node (a `stack`, `list`, `code`, `markdown`…) that should take it, set `"grow": true` on the node itself (next to `type`, not in `props`): expanded it fills the height and scrolls inside. Mark one node; the rest stay at their natural size, top-aligned.

stack.description: Lays children out in a row or column.

grid.description: Equal-width columns that wrap onto rows.

card.description: A bordered panel with an optional title and description.

text.description: A line or paragraph of plain text.

markdown.description:
Markdown text (GitHub flavoured), read as MDX and drawn as data (nothing runs): frontmatter folded, imports and comments hidden, `{braces}` as text, simple HTML (`
`, ``) and common docs components (Admonition, Tabs, Steps, Cards, details) drawn natively.

code.description: A block of code or command output.

badge.description: A short label, e.g. a status.

stat.description: A headline number with a label and optional change.

chart.description: A bar, line, area or dumbbell chart over one x field and up to 5 series on a single y axis (never two y scales; put measures of different scale in separate charts). bar compares amounts, line shows a trend, area a trend of parts (stacked), dumbbell two values per category (before → after, poll → result) as two dots joined by a line. Always shows a legend for 2+ series and lets the user flip to a table of the data. More than 5 series: keep the biggest and fold the rest into an "Other" series. Colours come from the theme and are checked for colour-blind safety; you can't set them. At most 2,000 rows.

data.description: Rows, e.g. [{ month: "Jan", api: 120, web: 80 }]. At most 2,000.

x.description: Field of each row used for the x axis (a dumbbell's rows).

series.description: [{ key, label }] — fields plotted as series, in a fixed order. A dumbbell takes exactly 2: before, then after.

unit.description: Suffix for values. Symbols and magnitude suffixes attach to the number ("k" → 16k, "M", "%", "°", "°C"; a currency symbol leads: $12); a word gets a space ("ms" → 42 ms); a leading space you write is kept (" pts" → 12 pts).

zero.description: line and area: start the value axis at 0. Default: bars and stacks always start at 0; lines and unstacked areas fit their data (padded to nice ticks, with any refs), and include 0 only when the data crosses it.

domain.description: line and area: [low, high] for the value axis, e.g. [0, 100] for a percentage. Widened if the data or a ref falls outside.

height.description: Pixels. Default 240 (a horizontal dumbbell sizes itself: 28px a row).

refs.description: Reference lines, at most 20: [{ axis: "y", value: 0, label: "Tie" }]. axis "y" is a value (a target, zero), "x" a category; label at most 40 characters, drawn outside the plot (beside a horizontal line, above a vertical one), never over the data.

orientation.description: bar and dumbbell only. Default: a dumbbell is horizontal, bars turn horizontal when a category name is long.

labels.description: Direct labels. Default "ends" for line, area (each series' last value) and dumbbell (the gap at the row end); "none" for bar ("ends" puts each bar's value, or a stack's total, at its tip). "all" labels every point: rarely right.

sort.description: Row order. "value": biggest first (bar, dumbbell by its second series). "gap": a dumbbell's widest gap first. Default "none", the data's order.

scale.description: dumbbell only: how dots are coloured. { type: "sequential" | "diverging" | "categorical", domain?: [low, high], midpoint?, bins?: 2-7, unit? }. Default: two shades of one hue. "diverging" colours each dot by its own value's side of the midpoint (the first series hollow) with a legend of the bins (dots carry at most 5 bins; more are merged): for signed values such as margins (poll → result, -3 to +5); for before → after of raw values (points, prices) use the default or "categorical", which uses the first two series colours.

diagram.description: A Mermaid diagram: sequence, flowchart (architecture, network, service maps, data flows), entity-relationship, state, class, gantt. `text` is Mermaid source. Themed with the app (light and dark), sanitised, no click handlers.

map.description: A map. `kind` picks the form: "markers" (the default) is a street map (OpenStreetMap tiles) with labelled markers, for "where on the streets"; "choropleth" colours regions by one value each (a value per country or state); "bubble" sizes a circle at each place by its value (a value at a point: revenue by city); "outline" is a plain map with highlighted regions and marked places; "connection" draws links between places as great-circle arcs, as wide as their value (flights between hubs, traffic between data centres); "hexbin" bins many raw points into hexagons coloured by how many fall in each (or the sum or mean of a weight). The region kinds draw bundled geometry (`region`: world, europe, us-states), work offline, follow the theme, label small sets directly, and flip to a table. Region ids are what you'd write: ISO alpha-3 ("PRT"), alpha-2 ("PT") or an English name for countries; postal code ("PA"), FIPS or name for US states. An unknown id is refused with the nearest names. Colours come from the theme; you can't set them.

markers.description: markers only, required there: [{ id?, lat, lng, label, detail?, tone?: 'default'|'success'|'warning'|'danger' }], at most 2,000. `id` lets a route in `lines` name the marker.

center.description: markers only: [lat, lng]. Default: fit all markers.

lines.description: markers only: routes, [{ points, label?, detail?, tone? }], at most 50; `points` is 2 to 1,000 places in order, each [lat, lng] or a marker's `id`. Drawn as lines on the street map, named for the keyboard.

cluster.description: markers only: "auto" (default: close markers group into a numbered cluster from 40 markers, ringed in the worst status), true, or false. Enter or a click on a cluster zooms in.

hubs.description: connection, required: [{ id, label, lon, lat, detail? }], at most 100; ids unique (text up to 40 characters, or a whole number).

links.description: connection, required: [{ from, to, value?, label?, detail? }] between hub ids, at most 200; no self-links, one row per pair (per direction when `directed`). `value` (0 or more) sets the width.

directed.description: connection: arrowheads from `from` to `to`. Default false.

width.description: connection: lines as wide as their value (default when any link has one) or all one width.

radius.description: hexbin: the hexagon's radius, 8 to 40 px. Default 16.

aggregate.description: hexbin: what a cell's colour says: how many points (default), or the sum or mean of their `weight`.

missing.description: choropleth: how regions without a row look: hatched as "no data", or plain land (outside the data, as for 14 swing states on a US map). Default: hatched while at most half the set lacks a row, else land. A null value is always hatched.

region.description: Region kinds: the bundled geometry. Default "world". "europe" is the countries of Europe (with Türkiye, Cyprus and the Caucasus), at a scale where Malta and Luxembourg show.

data.description: choropleth, required: [{ id, value, label?, detail? }], one row per region, at most 3,000. `value` is a number, or null for "no data" (hatched, never the lowest class).

highlight.description: outline: [{ id, label?, detail?, tone? }], at most 100 regions to mark; `tone` 'default'|'success'|'warning'|'danger' is also said in words.

points.description: bubble, required: [{ lon, lat, value (0 or more), label, detail?, shade? }], at most 500, area proportional to value, the biggest labelled where they fit. outline: [{ lon, lat, label, detail?, tone? }], at most 200. hexbin, required: [{ lon, lat, weight? }], at most 5,000 raw points.

scale.description: choropleth, hexbin (sequential or diverging) and bubble `shade`: { type: "sequential" | "diverging" | "categorical", domain?: [low, high], midpoint?, bins?: 2-7, unit? }. Default sequential, 5 classes. Values past the domain go in the end classes (labelled "< low", "> high"); without a domain, outliers are fenced off the same way.

view.description: Region kinds: "auto" (default: the region set, or for bubble, connection and hexbin the places, ignoring the far-off ones from 20 places, with "N outside view") or [west, south, east, north] in degrees. A world view narrower than about 50° by 35° draws the detailed (1:50m) coast.

title.description: Region kinds: what the map shows, at most 120 characters; its accessible name and the table's caption.

legend.description: Region kinds: true (default) or { title } (at most 80 characters), e.g. { title: "Margin (R + / D -)" }.

labels.description: Region kinds. "auto" (default): every label for 12 or fewer items, else the regions whose label fits inside them, up to 10 of the biggest bubbles and 12 of the busiest hubs where they don't collide, and link labels up to 40 links; "all" up to 24 (hexbin: each cell's value, from radius 16); "none".

noDataLabel.description: choropleth: the legend's word for regions without a row (hatched or land, see `missing`). Default "No data" (hatched) or "Not in the data" (land).

maxRadius.description: bubble: the largest bubble's radius, 6 to 48 px. Default about a twelfth of the map's short side.

unit.description: bubble, connection, hexbin: suffix for values, as on charts ("M EUR", "%", " flights", " stations").

borders.description: outline: draw borders between regions (default) or not.

height.description: Pixels, 160 to 900. Default 320 for markers, 360 for region kinds. Expanded, the map fills the dialog.

flow.description: A flow graph. "sankey": quantities flowing from stage to stage (CI jobs through lint, test and build to passed or failed; requests through services; cost by step), bands as wide as their values, flowing one way (a cycle is refused). "network": things and the links between them (service calls, package dependencies), laid out by force, up to a few hundred nodes. Both label small graphs directly, take arrows node to node (Enter steps along a node's links), and flip to a table (sankey: source, target, value; network: each node's neighbours). Ids and labels are text. Colours come from the theme.

nodes.description: [{ id, label? }] (ids unique, at most 60 characters). sankey also takes tone?: 'default'|'success'|'warning'|'danger' (e.g. a failed stage), at most 200 nodes. network takes group? (at most 3 groups, coloured) and size? (node weight), at most 500 nodes.

links.description: [{ source, target, value, label? }] between node ids. sankey: value above 0, at most 1,000 links, no cycles. network: value optional (line weight), at most 2,000 links.

unit.description: Suffix for values, as on charts (" jobs", "ms", "$").

title.description: What the graph shows, at most 120 characters: its accessible name and the table's caption.

labels.description: Node labels. "auto" (default): every sankey node; network: all up to 40 nodes, else the 12 most connected.

height.description: Pixels, 160 to 900. Default 320 (sankey), 360 (network). Expanded, it fills the dialog.

timer.description: A live clock that ticks in the app without you re-rendering: a countdown `until` a time (e.g. a cron's next run) or elapsed time `since` one (e.g. a sub-agent that is running). Times are ISO 8601 or epoch milliseconds.

done.description: Shown when a countdown reaches zero. Without it, the timer shows "overdue 3m 12s" and keeps counting, in a danger colour.

live.description: Keeps its children fed with data the app reads itself (see `sources`), refreshed every `every` ms without you re-rendering. Children bind the latest result as {{data}} (or the name in `as`), and with `history: N` the last N samples as {{history}}: [{ t: "14:03:21", …the numeric fields of each sample }] for charts over time. Shows when it last updated, and errors in place.

source.description: A source, e.g. { kind: "system" } or { kind: "postgres.query", connection: "shop", sql: "select …" }.

every.description: Refresh interval in ms (minimum 1000). Omit to read once (with a refresh button).

as.description: Name to bind the latest result to. Default "data".

form.description: Collects the user's input. Put inputs (textfield, choice, select, slider, rank, toggle) and any layout inside; it adds the submit button. Values stay in the app while the user edits (no message per click). On submit the form locks and shows the answer: with ui_ask the values come straight back to you as JSON; with ui_render they arrive as the user's next message.

textfield.description: A text answer. `multiline` for longer text (e.g. a reply the user edits before it is sent).

name.description: Key of this value in the answer.

choice.description: Pick one option (or several with `multiple`), shown as selectable cards with optional descriptions. Give `correct` (a value or list) for a quiz: once answered, right and wrong picks are marked and `explanation` is shown.

select.description: Pick one from a dropdown, for longer option lists.

slider.description: A number in a range (budget, effort, confidence, priority).

rank.description: Order items by priority (drag or use the arrows). The answer is the list of values, first = most important.

table.description: Rows of data under column headers. Cells are strings or numbers. Columns sort when clicked; tables over 8 rows get a filter box, so pass all the rows rather than a sample.

empty.description: Shown when there are no rows.

find.description: Fill the filter box: shows only rows containing this, so you can point the user at specific rows. Update it in place (same ui_render id) to point elsewhere.

kv.description: Label/value pairs, e.g. details of one item.

list.description: A bulleted or numbered list of strings.

diff.description: A file change shown as removed/added lines.

link.description: Opens a URL in the browser.

button.description: A button. `prompt` sends that text to you (the agent) as the user's next message; `draft` puts text in the user's message box for them to edit and send; `href` opens a URL. Give exactly one. A `prompt` that differs from `label` is shown to the user to confirm before it is sent.

collapsible.description: A section the user can expand.

tabs.description: Tabbed sections. Children must be `tab` nodes.

image.description: An image, e.g. a screenshot. `src` is an https: or data: URL, or the absolute path of an image file (png, jpg, gif, webp, svg) inside this chat's folders or the system temp folder.

browser.description: A live, interactive preview of a web page in a browser frame. `src` is an http(s) URL (e.g. a dev server on localhost) or the absolute path of a self-contained .html file inside this chat's folders. The page runs sandboxed. A local .html file shows at once; any URL waits for the user to click Load, showing them the full URL.

patch.description: A unified diff, e.g. the output of `git diff`, shown per file with hunks and added/removed lines.

diffreview.description: A multi-file diff to review and act on, one file at a time: a file list (status, +/−, a viewed tick; tabs across the top when narrow), j/k files, n/p hunks, v viewed, Enter opens the file. Each file and hunk has Ask about this and Ask to change or revert this (both draft into the composer, never applied), Copy path, Copy hunk and Open in editor. Tabs 4 wide, no wrapping (a wrap toggle wraps with a hanging indent). Prefer the `diff-review` component, which reads git.diff live.

text.description: A unified diff: `git diff` output, or git.diff's `text`.

files.description: git.diff's `files` ({ path, oldPath?, status, additions, deletions, binary }), for binary and renamed files the text can't show; else read from the text.

range.description: What the diff is of (e.g. main...HEAD): viewed ticks are kept per range.

truncated.description: The text was cut (git.diff's `truncated`); says so above the files.

name.description: Where the viewed ticks are kept in the UI's draft, so they survive re-renders and the agent can read them with ui_get_values. The diff-review component uses "viewed".

tests.description: Test results in green and red: counts, a pass/fail bar, failures first with their messages, passing tests folded away. Give the test command's raw output as `text` (cargo test, pytest -v, go test -v, jest, vitest, node --test, TAP, mix test, rspec); it is parsed here, so pass it as printed. Or give structured `results`.

text.description: Raw output of the test run.

results.description: Instead of text: [{ name, status: "pass"|"fail"|"skip", file?, duration? (ms), message? }].

find.description: Fill the filter (fuzzy on test name and file): shows the matching tests, e.g. the ones you just fixed.

filetree.description: A folder tree you can fold, with file counts per folder. `text` is what `tree` printed (`tree -F` marks folders reliably), or give `paths` (from find, git ls-files, rg --files). Big trees open two levels deep.

paths.description: Instead of text: file paths, one per item.

open.description: Levels open at first. Default: all for small trees, 2 for big ones.

find.description: Fill the search (fuzzy on names; on the path when it has a "/"): opens the folders down to the matches, hides the rest and marks them. Use it to show where something lives, e.g. "refund" or "src/billing/refund.rs".

json.description: JSON with syntax colours, folding and sizes. `text` is JSON as printed by jq, curl or a file (several documents in a row show as a list); or pass `value`. Large values open two levels deep.

value.description: Instead of text: any JSON value.

find.description: Fill the search: a key, a value, or a path like "customer.email" or "items.0.sku"; opens down to each match and marks it.

textfile.description: A file or long text for reading: what `cat`, `head` or `sed -n` printed. Fits the size: short text sits inline; longer text gets line numbers, a scroll box and search. `highlight` lines or a `find` scroll the view to them. With a `path`, Markdown renders (raw toggle), CSV/TSV shows as a table and JSON as `json`.

path.description: File path or name; picks the view and is shown as the title.

start.description: Number of the first line, e.g. 40 for `sed -n 40,80p`. Default 1.

follow.description: Keep the view scrolled to the last line as the text grows (logs).

find.description: Fill Find: marks every line containing it and scrolls to the first; the user steps through with Enter. Use with `highlight` to point at code.

wordcount.description: What `wc` printed, as a breakdown: totals, and a bar per file for the main count. Pass `columns` when not the default lines/words/bytes, e.g. ["lines"] for `wc -l`.

columns.description: Which counts each row holds, in order: "lines", "words", "bytes", "chars". Default ["lines","words","bytes"]; a single number per row means lines.

gitgraph.description: Git history as a graph: a colour per lane, refs (HEAD, branches, remotes, tags) as badges, then hash, subject, and author and date when present. `text` is what `git log --graph --oneline --decorate` printed (add --all for every branch; add --format="%h%d %s (%an, %ar)" for author and date).

gitstatus.description: `git status` grouped: branch with ahead/behind, then conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked files with a badge per change. `text` is what `git status --porcelain=v1 -b` printed (best), or plain `git status`.

diffstat.description: `git diff --stat` (or `git show --stat`, `git log --stat` for one commit) as a bar of additions and deletions per file, largest first.

sql.description: A SQL editor the user runs: syntax highlighting, completion of the connection's table and column names, ⌘↵ to run, results as a sortable table, a history of runs, and "Send to chat" to bring a query and its result back to you. Runs read-only (READ ONLY transaction, 15s timeout, row limit) on a saved connection. Give `sql` to start from; render again with the same id and new `sql` to rewrite it.

connection.description: A connection name from ui_catalog `connections`; the user can switch.

syntax.node: A node is a string (text), or { type, props?, children? } where type is a primitive or a library component name, or a control node.
syntax.bindings: Any string inside props or text can contain {{path}} to insert a value from the component's props (e.g. {{user.name}}, {{items.0}}). A string that is exactly "{{path}}" passes the value through unchanged, so arrays and numbers keep their type.
syntax.each: { each: "path.to.array", as: "item", index?: "i", key?: "id", children: [nodes] } repeats children once per element, with {{item}} and {{i}} bound. Give `key` (a field of each item) whenever the list can change or reorder between renders, so open sections and other UI state stay with their item.
syntax.if: { if: "path", children: [nodes], else?: [nodes] } renders children when the value is truthy (non-empty string/array, true, non-zero).
syntax.components: Using a library component as a node passes its props: { type: "deploy-status", props: { env: "{{env}}" } }.
syntax.libraries: Components from an installed component library are referenced by qualified name, library/name: { type: "acme/pr-card", props: { … } }. They are read-only; save your own variant under an unqualified name.

sources.about: Data the app reads itself. Use with a `live` node (and source_read to look first). GitHub, GitLab and Linear sources use the connections the user made in Settings → Integrations (read-only; you never see a token). Git sources read the folder of the chat the UI is in (yaah supplies it), or another of the chat's folders named by `repo` (its extra folders, its project's repos; anything else is refused, so call ui_request_folders first for a repo outside them), read-only, with refs and paths checked and output capped. Database sources take a `connection` name from ui_catalog `connections`; credentials never reach you.

system.returns: { host, uptimeSecs, cpu (%), cores: [%], memUsedGb, memTotalGb, memPct, swapUsedGb, load1, load5, load15, disks: [{ mount, totalGb, usedGb, pct }], processes: [{ pid, name, cpu, memGb }] (top 8 by CPU) }

docker.containers.returns: [{ id, name, image, state (running|exited|…), status, ports, created }]

docker.stats.returns: [{ name, cpu (%), memPct, memUsage, netIO, blockIO, pids }] (running containers)

postgres.schema.returns: { connection, tables: [{ schema, table, columns: [{ name, type, nullable }] }] }

postgres.query.returns: { connection, columns: [names in order], rows: [{ column: value }], truncated } — runs in a READ ONLY transaction with a 15s timeout

github.pr.returns: { number, title, url, body, state, stateLabel, draft, author, head, base, additions, deletions, changedFiles, review, reviewLabel, labels: [names], checks: [{ name, state: pass|fail|pending|skipped, tone, mark, url }] (failures first), checksSummary: { pass, fail, pending, skipped, text, tone }, reviews: [{ author, state, body, at }], comments: [{ author, body, at }], files: [{ path, additions, deletions }] }

github.pr.diff.returns: { repo, number, text (unified diff, for `patch`), bytes, truncated }

github.prs.returns: [{ number, title, url, author, branch, draft, review, checks (summary text), checksTone, updatedAt }]

github.issue.returns: { repo, number, ref ("owner/name#12"), title, url, body, state (open|closed), stateLabel (Open|Closed|Not planned), author, assignee, assignees: [logins], labels: [names], milestone, commentCount, comments: [{ author, body, at }] (the latest 30, oldest first), createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt, isPullRequest } — public repos work without a connection

params.limit: default 30, max 100 (pull requests are left out, so fewer may come back)

github.issues.returns: [{ number, title, url, state, stateLabel, author, assignee, labels: [names], comments (count), updatedAt }] — most recently updated first

params.iid: the issue's number in the project (required)

gitlab.issue.returns: { project, iid, ref ("group/project#7"), title, url, description, state (opened|closed), stateLabel (Open|Closed), author, assignee, assignees: [names], labels: [names], milestone, dueDate, commentCount, comments: [{ author, body, at }] (the latest 30 by people, oldest first; system notes left out), createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt }

params.project: full path; without it, issues across GitLab
params.scope: assigned_to_me (default without a project) | created_by_me | all (default with a project)

gitlab.issues.returns: [{ iid, ref, title, url, state, stateLabel, author, assignee, labels: [names], updatedAt }] — most recently updated first

linear.issue.returns: { id, title, url, description, state, stateType, priority, priorityVariant (for badge), estimate, due, assignee, creator, team, teamKey, cycle, project, labels: [names], subIssues: [{ id, title, state, done }], subDone, subTotal, links: [{ title, url }], comments: [{ author, body, at }] }

linear.issues.returns: [{ id, title, url, state, stateType, priority, priorityVariant, estimate, assignee, updatedAt }]

params.id: the project's slug id (the hex end of its URL, e.g. "3f9a1c2b7d4e") or UUID (required)

linear.project.returns: { id, uuid, name, url, description (its write-up, else the summary), summary, state, stateType, progressPct, lead, teams: [names], startDate, targetDate, updatedAt, issueCount, issuesDone, issues: [{ id, title, state, stateType, assignee, done }] (first 100) }

linear.board.returns: { team, teamKey, cycle, columnCount, columns: [{ state, type, count, issues: [rows as linear.issues] }] } — the active cycle's issues by workflow state (open issues when there is no cycle)

linear.cycle.returns: { team, number, name, starts, ends, daysLeft, progressPct, scope, completed, scopeAdded, issues, issuesDone, history: [{ day, scope, completed }] } — the active cycle

params.repo: optional: another of this chat's folders (absolute path or ~/…); default the chat's own folder
params.range: optional, e.g. "main...HEAD" or "HEAD~3" (default: the working tree, staged and not, against HEAD)
params.staged: true for the staged changes only (index against HEAD)
params.paths: optional [paths] relative to the repository read

git.diff.returns: { range, staged, text (unified diff, for `patch`/`diffreview`), files: [{ path, oldPath?, status: added|modified|deleted|renamed, additions, deletions, binary }], additions, deletions, truncated (text cut at 4 MB; files stay whole) }

params.repo: optional: another of this chat's folders (absolute path or ~/…); default the chat's own folder

git.log.returns: [{ sha, short, author, email, date (ISO 8601), subject, body }] — newest first; [] before the first commit

params.repo: optional: another of this chat's folders (absolute path or ~/…); default the chat's own folder

git.status.returns: { branch (null when detached), detached, oid, upstream, ahead, behind, clean, files: [{ path, oldPath?, index, worktree }] } — index/worktree: modified|added|deleted|renamed|copied|typechange|unmerged|untracked, or null when unchanged there

params.repo: optional: another of this chat's folders (absolute path or ~/…); default the chat's own folder
params.path: optional: the file at that revision instead of the commit

git.show.returns: { rev, path?, text (the commit with its patch, or the file), binary, truncated }
